title: Utility power loss
plain_text: The grid fails for seconds to days. IT shuts down when the battery runs out and cooling stops at once unless it is on UPS or generator.
covered_by: UPS ride-through (default 10 min), generator option with ATS, measured cooling ride-through (test E5), N+1/2N per profile.
customer_owns: Whether to buy the generator and fuel, the utility contract, and whether cooling is put on UPS.

title: Arc flash or electrical fault
plain_text: A fault while a panel is open or a component failure can injure someone and damage equipment.
covered_by: Arc-flash study and labels, selective coordination, listed dead-front gear, lockout points, NFPA 70E training at turnover.
customer_owns: Only qualified electricians work on it and the labels are followed.

title: Site fault current differs from assumption
plain_text: Until the utility gives its fault current and voltage, arc-flash labels and some ratings are provisional.
covered_by: Labels marked provisional until SAT; study updated with utility data; panel SCCR at least 65 kA.
customer_owns: Provide utility fault current and voltage before the unit ships.

title: Rack inlets run hot
plain_text: Hot days, a failed cooling unit or more load than planned push inlet temperatures up; IT throttles or trips.
covered_by: N+1 cooling, climate derate built into sizing, inlet sensors at three heights per rack with ASHRAE alarms, load-step and failover tests.
customer_owns: Keep IT load inside the configured kW, keep filters and coils clean, do not block containment.

title: Cooling stops when power is lost
plain_text: If cooling is not on UPS, inlet temperature in a small container rises several degrees per minute at full load.
covered_by: Ride-through measured in test E5 and published; option to put fans and pumps on UPS; generator start in 10 s; load-shed hooks.
customer_owns: Choose: accept a few minutes, add cooling to UPS, or add a generator.

title: Fire inside the container
plain_text: A cable, battery or power supply fire would mean loss of IT, an agent discharge and downtime.
covered_by: Very-early smoke detection, clean agent with 10-minute hold, HVAC shutdown, EPO, non-combustible liner, battery separation.
customer_owns: Fire marshal relationship, agent recharge contract, no combustible storage inside, insurance.

title: Lithium battery thermal runaway
plain_text: A battery cell failure can release flammable gas and start a fire that spreads if not contained.
covered_by: LFP chemistry, UL 1973/9540 listed cabinets with UL 9540A data, BMS alarms, gas detection and venting above 20 kWh, capped battery size on smaller tiers; BEN 2000 battery rooms with 2-hour separation and gas detection.
customer_owns: No unapproved batteries, keep BMS firmware updated, respond to BMS alarms.

title: Water or coolant leak
plain_text: Roof, door seals, condensate or a liquid-cooling loop can leak and damage IT.
covered_by: Rope leak sensors, condensate float alarm, drip trays, CDU auto pump stop on leak, propylene glycol only, seal inspection schedule.
customer_owns: Keep drains clear, respond to alarms, pad drainage.

title: Transport or lifting damage
plain_text: A bad lift or rough transport can twist the frame or crack a weld.
covered_by: Corner-casting lifts with spreader, PE-checked frame, shock loggers, set-down inspection, freight insurance; BEN 2000 modules lifted on engineered lugs with a 100 t crane and a certified lift plan.
customer_owns: Crane access, competent rigger, route survey for the high-cube height.

title: Wind, snow, seismic or flood above design
plain_text: An event beyond the design values could move the unit or let water in.
covered_by: PE anchorage to the climate wind speed, pad spec, flood elevation rule, hurricane louvres where needed.
customer_owns: Give us the true site conditions and build the pad to spec.

title: Intrusion into the controls network
plain_text: An attacker who reaches the controls LAN could change setpoints or stop cooling.
covered_by: IEC 62443 zones, isolated controls LAN, signed firmware, no inbound ports, outbound-only remote support that can be disabled, hardwired life safety.
customer_owns: The firewall between BEN controls and the customer LAN (unless managed), password handover, patch windows.

title: Vendor cloud dependence
plain_text: If a supplier disappears or changes terms, a cloud-dependent box loses its dashboard.
covered_by: Local-first design: everything runs on the gateway in the container; dashboard works with no internet; source escrow for white-label; CSV export any time.
customer_owns: Keep local backups (we automate to customer storage if provided).

title: Single component failure without redundancy
plain_text: With N cooling or a single gateway, one failure can mean a thermal event or loss of monitoring.
covered_by: Nodes buffer one hour and keep failsafe outputs, spare gateway image and spare node in the kit, cooling units run standalone, N+1/2N by profile.
customer_owns: Choosing N to save cost; keeping the spares kit on site.

title: Sensor drift gives false comfort
plain_text: A drifted sensor can make the dashboard look fine while the room is not.
covered_by: Redundant sensors, idle cross-check (test E1), drift detection, 12-month or trigger-based recalibration.
customer_owns: Allow calibration visits, do not move sensors.

title: Permit delay or unexpected AHJ requirement
plain_text: The local authority may classify the container as a building, ask for a field evaluation or more fire protection, and take longer than the build.
covered_by: Pre-application package, code summary, field-evaluation budget line, site requirements signed before build, parallel permit path in the schedule.
customer_owns: Pulling permits (or authorising us), zoning, neighbour relations.

title: Refrigerant rules change
plain_text: GWP limits and flammable-refrigerant rules are changing; a unit model can become unavailable for new installs.
covered_by: Non-flammable refrigerant under 700 GWP chosen now, or water loops; EPA 608 technicians; small charges.
customer_owns: Normal service contracts.

title: Noise complaints
plain_text: Dry coolers and condensers can exceed night-time limits at the property line.
covered_by: Sound prediction at quote, low-noise fans and night setback, acoustic survey at SAT (test E10), barrier option.
customer_owns: Site selection, setbacks, local ordinance.

title: Long-lead parts slip
plain_text: UPS, switchgear, cooling units and transformers can take months and slip.
covered_by: Long-lead orders at engineering release, approved alternates, stocked controls hardware.
customer_owns: Early deposit and configuration freeze; no late changes.

title: Component discontinued or listing changes
plain_text: A specified part may be discontinued or lose its listing before or after build.
covered_by: Approved alternates in the BOM, configuration freeze per unit, FAT repeats affected tests.
customer_owns: None.

title: Site costs above quote
plain_text: Civil works, permits and utility connection can cost more than the allowance.
covered_by: Firm box price after engineering release; site works quoted after survey; utility costs identified at survey.
customer_owns: Utility fees, civil works, permits, taxes, and changes after freeze.

title: Energy cost higher than expected
plain_text: Cooling energy rises in hot climates and with high utilisation.
covered_by: Honest PUE estimate from the configuration, measured at SAT (test E9), economizer and variable-speed fans.
customer_owns: Electricity tariff and IT utilisation.

title: Fuel or glycol spill
plain_text: A generator tank or coolant loop leak to ground brings clean-up cost and fines.
covered_by: Double-wall UL 142 tank, overfill alarm, SPCC plan where required, propylene glycol, drip trays.
customer_owns: Fuel deliveries, SPCC plan ownership, stormwater rules.

title: Person inside during agent discharge or refrigerant leak
plain_text: Clean agent or a refrigerant leak can disorient or expose a technician inside.
covered_by: Pre-discharge alarm with delay, abort switch, door interlock, refrigerant detector, purge ventilation, written entry procedure, non-flammable refrigerants.
customer_owns: Follow the entry procedure, keep training current.

title: Heat and noise in the hot aisle
plain_text: Technicians can face heat stress and noise above 85 dBA behind high-density racks.
covered_by: Work limits in the O&M manual, hearing protection signage, cold-aisle work position for most tasks.
customer_owns: Work-rest cycles and PPE.

title: No Uptime Tier certification is claimed
plain_text: We design with TIA-942 Rated-2/3 concepts but do not hold a Tier certificate; an insurer or auditor may ask.
covered_by: Design-basis statement, FAT/SAT evidence, optional third-party audit at cost.
customer_owns: Deciding if a certification is required and paying for it.

title: Relocation and CSC validity
plain_text: A modified container cannot ship by sea or rail as a container without re-certification, and a new site needs new permits.
covered_by: Relocation procedure, re-certification path through a classification society, new anchorage calc.
customer_owns: New site survey, permits and freight.

title: Medium-voltage utility service lead time (BEN 2000)
plain_text: A new 12.47 kV service with primary metering and two pad-mount transformers is utility work on the utility's schedule, typically 26 to 52 weeks.
covered_by: Interconnection application filed at order, utility window carried on the critical path, load letter and single-line ready at kick-off, temporary 480 V service for commissioning where allowed.
customer_owns: The utility contract and fees, land for utility equipment, easements.

title: Water availability for adiabatic cooling (BEN 2000)
plain_text: Hot-day make-up water is 2 to 8 cubic metres a day per 1,000 kW; drought rules or a weak supply can force the coolers to run dry and lose capacity on the hottest days.
covered_by: Dry mode below 28 C, chilled-water option for hot climates, water quantity and drain confirmed at site survey, storage tank option, water management plan per ASHRAE 188.
customer_owns: Water supply contract, drought-rule compliance, sewer discharge permit for bleed water.

title: Module joint leakage (BEN 2000)
plain_text: The three hall modules are sealed on site; the seams are the one part of the IP66 envelope not finished in the factory.
covered_by: Factory compression gaskets and field EPDM cover strips with a drained cavity, joint seal hose test E15 at SAT and after any relocation, leak rope under each joint, semi-annual seal inspection.
customer_owns: Keep the roof clear of debris and snow beyond design, respond to alarms.

title: Construction permit for a building (BEN 2000)
plain_text: The hall is a building (IBC Group B or F-1), not an equipment enclosure: plan review, state modular approval and inspections take 8 to 16 weeks before civil works can start.
covered_by: Stamped permit set from the engineering release, state modular label on each module, pre-application meeting, civil package starts after permit, both occupancy classifications budgeted.
customer_owns: Zoning, land use, easements, neighbour notice, permit fees.

title: Flood above the pad
plain_text: A flood above the pad puts water in the enclosure and takes the unit out for a long time.
covered_by: Pad 0.3 m above base flood elevation on every tier; hardening H2 and H3 add a 600 mm flood plinth with sealed penetrations, and the IP66 envelope holds against splash and standing water; flood alarm on the plinth.
customer_owns: Site selection outside the floodway, true flood zone data, choosing H2 where the map says so.

title: Ballistic or forced-entry attack
plain_text: Gunfire or a break-in can destroy IT, injure people or take data-bearing equipment.
covered_by: H1: steel skin, keyed access, door contacts. H3: UL 752 ballistic panels (level 3 to 8), ASTM F3038 forced-entry doors, IK10, mantrap vestibule, two-factor access, tamper detection on the PLC and an audit trail in BEN Care.
customer_owns: Threat assessment and choice of level, guard force and response, perimeter.

title: Electromagnetic pulse or interference
plain_text: A HEMP or intentional electromagnetic interference event can take out IT and controls electronics across the site at once.
covered_by: Surge protection, shielded controls cabling and fibre to the outside on every unit; H3 shielding option: 80 dB enclosure per MIL-STD-188-125-1 with filtered penetrations, shield integrity tested annually, TEMPEST-ready separation (TEMPEST certification not claimed).
customer_owns: Deciding whether the threat justifies the option, the certified TEMPEST authority if required.
